bib.title: Wizard of Wikipedia: Knowledge-Powered Conversational Agents
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v2, 21 Feb 2019; ICLR 2019 per ledger)

read.skipped: Appendix A.1 (UI image), B.2 and B.3 have headings only in the text; no body text.

question: Can open-domain dialogue agents be built that retrieve Wikipedia knowledge, select and condition on it, and produce knowledgeable, engaging replies, and how can this be measured?
hypothesis: Explicit memory over retrieved knowledge (Transformer Memory Networks) beats models that must memorise knowledge in weights.
contributions: Wizard of Wikipedia dataset: crowd-sourced human-human dialogues with each wizard turn linked to a Wikipedia sentence
Transformer Memory Network architectures in retrieval and generative (end-to-end and two-stage) versions
Knowledge dropout, a novel training technique
Automatic and human evaluation, with a public benchmark in ParlAI

method.summary: A crowd-sourced dataset of wizard-apprentice dialogues where the wizard sees TF-IDF-retrieved Wikipedia passages and marks the sentence used. Models retrieve candidates with the same IR system, attend over them with a Transformer encoder and either rank stored responses or generate one with a Transformer decoder.
method.task: knowledge-grounded open-domain dialogue (knowledge selection plus response retrieval or generation)

datasets.name: Wizard of Wikipedia
datasets.split: train 166,787 utterances / 18,430 dialogues; valid 17,715 / 1,948; test seen 8,715 / 965; test unseen 8,782 / 968
datasets.preprocessing: wizard-chosen sentence recorded per turn; 'no sentence used' chosen 6.2% of the time; about 61 knowledge candidates per turn

datasets.name: Wikipedia knowledge base
datasets.preprocessing: articles flattened to sentences, each prepended with article title

datasets.name: SQuAD
datasets.preprocessing: used as additional multi-task training for the Transformer

models.name: Retrieval Transformer Memory Network
models.architecture: Transformer encoder for context and each knowledge sentence, dot-product attention over knowledge added to context encoding; separate Transformer encodes candidate responses; cosine-style score over normalised vectors

models.name: Generative End-to-end Transformer Memory Network
models.architecture: shared Transformer encoder; attention picks best knowledge m_best; its encoding concatenated with dialogue encoding into Transformer decoder; BPE

other.loss: L = (1 - lambda) L_NLL + lambda L_knowledge (lambda value not stated)

models.name: Generative Two-stage Transformer Memory Network
models.architecture: separately trained knowledge selector (best Transformer from Table 2) and utterance generator; dialogue and knowledge re-encoded after selection

models.name: Baselines: Random, IR baseline (word overlap), BoW MemNet, Transformer without knowledge, repeat-last-utterance

training.objective: retrieval: cross-entropy with other batch examples' responses as negatives; generative: negative log-likelihood, optionally plus cross-entropy on knowledge attention weighted by lambda
training.dropout: knowledge dropout (K.D.): model is prevented from attending to knowledge a fraction of the time during training (fraction not stated)

other.pretraining: Transformer pretrained on Reddit then fine-tuned on the task; SQuAD multi-tasking variant

inference.decoding: beam search of 5 for generative models
inference.samples: single output per turn; no seeds or repeated runs stated
inference.retrieval: TF-IDF inverted index with hashing trick (Chen et al. 2017 DrQA retriever); three queries per turn (topic x1, last two turns xt and xt-1); top 7 articles (first paragraph only) per query; results flattened to sentences with article title prepended; for the original topic, article first 10 sentences shown to human wizards

other.retrieval_candidates: retrieval models rank gold response among 99 random candidates (R@1); response candidate set is training-set utterances

metrics.name: Recall@1 (R@1)
metrics.definition: rank of gold (response or knowledge sentence); for responses among 99 random candidates

metrics.name: Unigram F1
metrics.definition: unigram overlap of prediction with gold response (or gold knowledge in Table 2)

metrics.name: Engagingness rating
metrics.definition: human rating of how much they liked the conversation

metrics.name: Wiki F1
metrics.definition: F1 overlap of model utterances with first 10 sentences of the Wikipedia page for the chosen topic, a proxy for knowledge used

eval.protocol: Automatic metrics on test seen and unseen with predicted and gold knowledge. Human eval: crowd workers chat 3-5 turns on a topic chosen from 2-3, rate 1-5; 546 conversations from 464 distinct workers incl. 100 human-human; Student's t-test, p<.05 / p<.01. Error analysis on 20 conversations per setting.

limits: Retriever is a fixed TF-IDF system; learning retrieval jointly is left to future work.
No training hyperparameters (optimizer, lr, batch size, model sizes, epochs, hardware, seeds) are given in the paper.
Human eval uses 3-5 turns per chat and crowd raters; retrieval models rated more engaging than generative ones, gap to humans remains.
Error analysis finds knowledge-conditioned models give fluent but wrong facts, e.g. listing places in Greece when asked about Ireland; no hallucination rate is measured.
Metrics are word-overlap against one human reply; 2018-scale models.
